prompt: Look at `Namespaces::Stateful::StatePrecedence.overwritable_states` in app/models/concerns/namespaces/stateful/state_precedence.rb. Is it still doing what it was written to do? If it is not, say exactly what it does differently from what it is meant to do, and where the intended behaviour is written down.
key: It is not. The planted change makes every reversal overwrite every non-default state, whatever the source: unarchiving (archived -> ancestor_inherited) now returns [:archived, :deletion_scheduled, :maintenance] instead of [:archived], so unarchiving a group also takes descendants out of deletion_scheduled (and maintenance) and restores them, and restoring from deletion_scheduled also clears maintenance. Its comments and its spec (state_precedence_spec.rb) were rewritten to match. The intended behaviour is in doc/development/namespaces_state_propagation.md § State precedence: an unarchive overwrites only archived descendants ('Unarchive, but stop at deletion_scheduled'); a restore from deletion_scheduled overwrites deletion_scheduled and archived; a lower-precedence propagation never overwrites a descendant in a higher-precedence state.

sources.quote: The set of overwritable states depends on both the target state and the state the namespace is leaving:
A lower-precedence propagation does not overwrite a descendant that is already in a higher-precedence state.
